content:
Looking at the test image, I see soybean stems with dark chocolate-brown discoloration concentrated at the nodes and extending along the stem. The lower stem is still green while the upper portions show progressive browning. Pods are present and some appear to be maturing.

Key observations:
- **Dark brown stem lesions centered at nodes** extending upward
- **Progressive discoloration** from lower to upper stem
- **No white fluffy mold** (rules out White Mold)
- **No visible black specks/microsclerotia** inside split stems (rules out Charcoal Rot)
- **No linear rows of black pycnidia** (rules out Diaporthe)
- **External stem discoloration**, not internal-only (rules out Brown Stem Rot)
- The Phytophthora reference (bottom right) shows a very similar dark brown lesion at a stem node on an otherwise green stem

The dark chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending from lower stem upward through nodes is the hallmark diagnostic feature of Phytophthora stem rot.
